sources.title: A bunch of Grand Theft Auto games will be cheap on Steam until GTA 6 comes out, and only one sucks
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's November 19 launch, Rockstar has multiple classic Grand Theft Auto games on sale on Steam – and, nearest I can tell, only on Steam. The Nintendo Switch eShop actually has a competing deal for the Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition Trilogy, which is down 67% to $19.79, but that sale ends in 11 hours from the time of writing. On Steam, several GTA games are discounted until November 19 for an obviously timed special promotion. On Steam, you'll find four games on sale via two actual products: You can't argue with GTA 4 for $6, but you might argue with this version of, in particular, GTA 3. The Definitive Edition Trilogy was famously panned at launch for wonky graphics and poor technical performance that, for the most part, has been patched up in the years since. However, the PC port for GTA 3's Definitive Edition is uniquely poorly rated for reasons that will sound familiar. Here's how the three games in this trilogy compare in Steam reviews: The reception to the two other games in the trilogy improved over time while GTA 3 steadily declined. Much like the day-one reviews, today's Steam players complain of Rockstar launcher interference, bugs, shoddy art, broken cinematics, and performance dips. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Curiously, perhaps unrelated to the quality of the port, some of today's gamers also don't seem to take too kindly to GTA 3's design sensibilities, it being slightly older than Vice City and San Andreas, and certainly a rawer open-world experience. Thomas Williamson, the CEO of the outsourced trilogy's original developer, Grove Street Games, said earlier this year that the criticism faced at launch was deserved. "I agreed with most of the people's reactions," he said. "But unfortunately, I feel like we did not agree with how the game was released and the response to it from a development side. And I think that would have changed the narrative significantly." However, he added, "at the end of the day, looking at the behind-the-scenes metrics on those games, there were a lot of people who were playing them and really enjoying them." You won't find Grove Street Games listed on the store pages for these games anymore. Previously, Williamson called it a "dick move" for Rockstar to have Grove Street's name removed. sources.title: Rockstar's having a sale on old GTA games on the only platform Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't coming to (ours)
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 finally arrives on November 19, but not for us, no—the big day is only for gamers on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. We're not being completely excluded, though: We can't have GTA 6 in November, but we can take advantage of pre-release discounts on a bunch of older GTA games—deals that, ironically, don't appear to be available on consoles. As noted by GamesRadar , there are four GTA games available in two releases: Grand Theft Auto 3, Vice City, and San Andreas bundled up in the GTA Trilogy for $19.79/£19.79/€19.79—67% off the regular price—and Grand Theft Auto 4: Complete Edition , which includes The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony expansions, for $6/£5.09/€6, a 70% discount. Those aren't the deepest discounts ever seen, but Grand Theft Auto games typically don't venture into the 90% off territory we all enjoy so much—and according to Isthereanydeal.com, this is as low as the GTA Trilogy has ever gone, and close to the mark for GTA 4 . You may recall that the GTA Trilogy Definitive Edition was a mess when it launched in 2021, but it seems to have turned that frown upside-down since then: On Steam, where the trilogy arrived in 2023, Vice City and San Andreas both hold "very positive" ratings. GTA 3 is stuck at a "mixed" rating, which is unfortunate: Glancing at user reviews, it sounds like the game still isn't in perfect shape, but it's also suffering from the fact that it's 25 years old, and was the first 3D game in the series—some jank and roughness was there right from the start. Grand Theft Auto 4: The Complete Edition, on the other hand, doesn't suffer from those shortcomings. It's getting pretty long in the tooth too—it came out in 2008—but represents a shift in design and tone that led the series into what it is today. If you're looking for just one older GTA game to horse around with, this is the one, especially given that it's less than half the cost of the trilogy. As mentioned, these sale prices are currently only being offered on Steam: There's currently no sign of any of them on either the Xbox or PlayStation stores (Fun fact: there actually is no digital version of GTA 4 on the PS Store because Sony didn't start selling full-priced games online until well after 2008). Maybe it's just coincidence, but they do appear to be intentional pre-GTA 6 sales: The discounts are on until November 19, when Grand Theft Auto 6 launches—except on PC. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Physical Copies Are Officially in the Wild
sources.text: Code in box editions have started to arrive With preloads for Grand Theft Auto 6 just around the corner, Rockstar Games has sent the code-in-box editions to retailers, so stores can deliver them to customers on time. Shipments have started to arrive, giving us a first look at the physical edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 . Fans who have pre-ordered Grand Theft Auto 6 can preload the game starting next week to ensure that they're able to launch it as soon as it's released in their region. PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X players who bought GTA 6 through their console's digital storefront can preload it starting Nov. 10 at midnight. However, those who ordered the code-in-box edition will have to wait until Thursday. As players get ready to pick up their physical editions of GTA 6 , local retailers have started preparing for the onslaught of gamers bound to rush to stores on Nov. 12. Shipments have seemingly arrived at MediaMarkt stores in Germany, and the retailer was quick to show the physical edition of Grand Theft Auto 6 on its Instagram stories . Thanks to this, we were able to get a first look at the poster that will be given to those who pre-ordered the game. An employee also shared a close-up of the exterior of the box, revealing the official game description, screenshots of Jason, Lucia, and Leonida, and labels such as online support and in-game purchases. Players perked up at the thought of online support, though at this point, it likely refers to mini-game leaderboards rather than GTA Online . We've known for months that GTA 6 is set to release on Nov. 19. Nevertheless, it's still hard for some to believe that launch day is nearly, finally here. The fact that people are now able to hold Grand Theft Auto 6 in their hands (even though physical editions don't actually include a disc ) makes this whole thing feel even more real.

sources.title: Square Enix accidentally botches a Nier: Automata update, balloons required file size from 50GB to 366GB on PC
sources.text: "Do you think games are silly little things?" Yesterday, Nier: Automata received a new patch on Steam, adding more language support to the title - it can now be played with Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese options - but this new update also, somehow, inflated the file size of the game on PC from about 50GB to 366GB. D'oh! What's worse is, the update is not optional. The cause of this, reportedly, is a bug that caused all the DLC in the YoRHa Edition of the game to become the same size as the base game - and the new download stacks them all concurrently. "Only SquareEnix can turn 40GB into 366GB with 8GB patch," says one dissatisfied Steam reviewer. If you don't have space for this massive new file on your PC (and I can't say I blame you, it's ridiculous), there is a workaround, as confirmed by Square Enix in a tweet via its Japanese Twitter account . "We have confirmed an issue where, following the latest update to the Steam version of Nier: Automata, the installation process indicates that more storage space is required than expected," noted the publisher. "We are currently investigating the cause and working on a solution. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game by unchecking the DLC under Steam → Properties → DLC." It's quite ironic, really, that so many Steam reviewers are complaining about things like "I just need to delete 90% of my computer to install this" when a large part of the game is managing the software/programmes installed on your android protagonists in order to upgrade your abilities and stats. There's even an ending for uninstalling your OS on your mechanical main characters. I'd be inclined to suggest this is some sort of meta psy-op from creator Yoko Taro , but… nah, that's just fantasy, isn't it? Isn't it? Speaking of Taro, earlier this year we learned that " Nier Automata will continue ", though we only heard back in 2025 tha t most of the projects the developer was working on were cancelled . One of these may have been the Tencent -backed Nier mobile game in 2024, which reportedly "struggled to find a monetisation to offset its high costs ."

sources.title: Nier: Automata developer is 'currently investigating' a bizarre update bug that drastically inflated the game's file size from 50GB to 366GB
sources.text: Square Enix is 'working to resolve the issue'. Usually, it's a good thing when a patch makes an already excellent game substantially larger. But in the case of Nier: Automata 's most recent update, bigger is most certainly not better. On Friday, the beloved action RPG from Square Enix received what should have been a straightforward update to add localisation support for Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Korean languages. But as reported by Automaton Media, the update also increased the game's file size from 50 gigabytes to a staggering 366 (and a half) gigabytes. "We have identified an issue following the latest update for Nier: Automata … where installation requires significantly more storage space than intended," wrote Square Enix in a Steam post . "We are currently investigating the cause and working to resolve the issue. We apologise for the inconvenience." It isn't clear how this issue has occurred, but it may be related to Nier: Automata's DLC. When selected for download on Steam, each DLC appears to have the same file size as the base game. Weirdly though, this is only true for the initial download and installation. Once the game is installed, the file reportedly reverts to a more appropriate size of roughly 50 gigs. Indeed, as a temporary solution, Square Enix suggests that anyone who needs to download Nier: Automata deselects all eight DLC when they do so. "As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game using the intended amount of storage space by going to "Properties" à "DLC" in Steam and unchecking each DLC item." While 366 gigabytes is obviously a ridiculous size for a game, what's frightening to me is that games are on track to become that massive in the coming years. Big budget games regularly exceed the 100 gigabytes in file size these days, while several major titles like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, have surpassed 200GB. One of the largest reported installations to date is for the combat simulator DCS World , which had a maximum file size of 250GB back in 2021 . Japanese Rural Life Adventure is a relaxing slow-life simulation where you can experience the charm of traditional Japanese countryside living, all in a beautifully crafted pixel-art world. Live in the Japanese Countryside Surrounded by Nature Fix up an old house, make the yard nice, grow your own crops, and become self-sufficient. Start by clearing the overgrown weeds, cleaning the floors, and repairing the “shoji” paper screens. By the time you’ve completed the tutorial, you’ll have learned the basics of village life. sources.title: How to trade all the Masks from the Happy Mask Shop in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: The Skull Mask, the Spooky Mask, the Bunny Hood, and more are part of the Happy Mask Shop quest in OOT Remake The Happy Mask Shop in Zelda Ocarina of Time has you run around Hyrule trading masks with characters for Rupees, including the Skull Mask, Spooky Mask, Bunny Hood, and the Keaton mask. Though these masks only serve as commodities to be traded with specific characters, if you can allocate all four to the right characters and complete this OOT quest, the Happy Mask Shop will give you access to four new masks that all have a very specific utility. Below I'll show you how to hand out all the Masks and the specific locations you need to look. Keep in mind that the Switch 2 version is the same as the original, in that the Happy Mask Shop won't open in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time until you open the passage to the Goron City. Fortunately, the guard who opens the passage will actually tell you that the Mask Shop is now open, flagging that you can start this questline. Bought from the Mask Shop for 10 Rupees, you need to give this to the Guard in Kakariko Village who opens the passage for you, the same one who lets you know that the Mask Shop is open. He'll give you 15 Rupees in return. Bought for 20 Rupees, head back to the starting area of Kokiri Village, where you start off and get the first Shield and Sword in Zelda Ocarina of Time , and turn North into the Lost Woods. sources.title: I Wouldn’t Dream of Playing the Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Right Now
sources.text: Some things are sacred. No, not like that! Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here . Unlike you, probably, I am not playing Nintendo's Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time right now. I even turned down a kind offer from my editor to review it. This despite the fact that it might be my favorite Zelda game (mostly by virtue of being the first one I played) and indubitably one of the greatest games ever — as close to a Citizen Kane as the medium has. I've read the ecstatic reviews , several of them by friends of mine, like Keza MacDonald and Christian Donlan, and of course Polygon's own Giovanni Colantonio, who I know to be people of good sense and great taste who share my reverence for this game and this series. I trust them. I also trust Nintendo, especially now it's clear the game was developed by the in-house Zelda team and not farmed out to an external studio. I trust producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, veterans of Zelda's golden age and architects of its great Breath of the Wild renaissance, who Gio talked to this week. I trust their decision to pass Ocarina on to younger developers at Nintendo to train and inspire them, but also to inject the aging game with youth and life. I also know that Ocarina needs the work. I played a little of the Nintendo 64 original recently, and while I remained entranced by its strangely haunted vibe , I found that, like so many early 3D games, it is fighting a battle with clunky, barely-ready technology that it has been slowly losing over the last 28 years. I'm honestly not sure that it's still fun to play now. And this matters to me, because my 10-year-old son loves Zelda — which, to him, means Tears of the Kingdom . He thinks Tears is the best game ever, and I wouldn't necessarily disagree. He's read the Ocarina of Time manga and fiddled about with other games in the series, including the Link's Awakening remake and The Wind Waker , but never settled into any of them. Honestly, I warned him off trying to play the original Ocarina . So the Ocarina remake arrives at a perfect time for him. He is beyond excited about it. He will get it, and his own Switch 2 to play it on, for Christmas. Put yourself in his shoes. (Maybe you once were, and got the original Ocarina , or the 3DS version, as a childhood Christmas gift yourself.) Can you imagine anything better? I just know that if I played the game before him, even surreptitiously, I would be stealing the magic of that moment. As desperate as I am to see the work of Aonuma and Fujibayashi's team, I can't countenance it. So I'll wait with him. Also… If I'm honest, maybe I'm not just doing it for him. Because I'll be unwrapping my own copy on Christmas morning. I'll be playing this magical game away from work, out of step with the discourse, in the cozy, contented, quiet bubble of the holidays, surrounded by my family. Maybe I'll feel like I'm 10, too. Like I said: can you imagine anything better? ZA/UM, the makers of Disco Elysium — well, some of them; it's complicated — return with another wonderfully funny, dark, and emotionally complex narrative RPG that uses tabletop dice rolls to enumerate the failings of human beings. One in particular: a not good, very bad spy who is trying to atone for a terrible betrayal. This 1988 NES classic from Capcom is simply one of the all-time great action platformers. It's all the more remarkable since the developers basically had to cobble it together in their spare time after the original was deemed a sales disappointment. Now Mega Man is a treasured franchise, and due for a return next year. I'm not playing Ocarina , but I am allowed to listen to the eight-track soundtrack sample that just dropped on Nintendo Music, and it's absolutely delicious. The exquisitely produced and performed new arrangements of Koji Kondo's immortal tunes are both a massive upgrade and resounding proof that Kondo had loaded his music with all this drama, humor, and sophistication from the start. Impossible to pick a favorite from the full flamenco of "Gerudo Valley," or the squawking penny whistles, accordions, oboes, and fiddles of "Market," or "Kakariko Village"'s plangeant harmonica. But let's go with the 10-minute "Hyrule Field Main Theme" for sheer epic sweep.

sources.text: Visual and performance issues not quite ironed out yet, which will be music to Nintendo's ears. sources.title: Nintendo exec says "new games and remakes both have a place" following Zelda: Ocarina of Time launch
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is finally out in the wild a good 28 years after Nintendo's original gem dropped back in 1998, and is already proving to be the highest-rated game of 2026 thus far. Sure, it's a remake, but it slots in nicely between all the other new games – and it's still just as valuable, too, as Nintendo senior vice president of product development and publishing Nate Bihldorff explains to Polygon . "I do think that new games and remakes both have a place in the Nintendo stable, of equal importance to be honest. There are fans of every single IP that we have out there," as he says. Remakes are very welcome to those fans, to say the least. "Of course, having new games in those series is wonderful, and I look forward to them as much as anyone else does, but there's also a deep satisfaction in revisiting games that were very, very special, like Ocarina of Time" – and that's evident in how well the remake is doing already, if you ask me. It made Metacritic's top 30 games of all time within a day, proving that the community is very much happy to enjoy remakes as it is entirely fresh titles. Longtime Legend of Zelda fans aren't the only people immersing themselves in Nintendo's revamped spin on Hyrule, either. As Bihldorff states, "It's also important to think about how many people had never played the original, and for them, the remake of Ocarina of Time is going to be an absolutely brand-new, 2026 experience, and one that I just cannot wait for them to get their hands on." A quick look at social media proves his assertion here right. Remakes don't just cater to old fans, but they help introduce countless more to long-standing franchises and series like The Legend of Zelda. They certainly don't take away from new releases, either – every fellow Zelda stan I know is on the edge of their seat waiting for more announcements from Nintendo, especially after the likes of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom . I don't see that changing, ever. While you're here, be sure to read our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review. sources.title: Ocarina of Time Remake Has the Best Water Temple, Aonuma Says
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda franchise producer Eiji Aonuma says the Ocarina of Time remake’s Water Temple is now the best version, thanks to one-button Iron Boots and a free camera. This remake of the legendary Nintendo 64 game isn’t the first time Nintendo has revisited the iconic Zelda title. Nintendo previously released an upgraded version on the Nintendo 3DS. However, third time’s the charm: Mr. Aonuma finally feels the water temple is at its best thanks to new upgrades in the Switch 2 version. He told Game Informer recently that the single-button ability to switch on the heavy iron boots and the improved camera control have made this the best version of the water temple. Another consideration compared to the original is that you couldn’t move the camera angle in the original game, and so if you were looking for a certain room in this 3D space relative to where you are now, it was much more difficult to orient yourself and think about the space where that room might exist. So I think those two together, you know, also with the heavy boots being one button press, I think this, for me, is the best version of the Water Temple. Other changes from Nintendo include removing Mario and Yoshi’s portraits from the original game. Nintendo also removed the Skyward Sword art added to the Nintendo 3DS remake. Aonuma says they removed these to maintain continuity. Plus, they no longer needed Easter eggs to promote a Wii U game release. [Laughs] I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I said, “Okay, sure.” But like earlier when we were talking about in the courtyard sequence with the Yoshi portrait. You know, you don’t want to interrupt the player’s experience by seeing something that’s unrelated to what they’re currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way. The remake is one of 2026’s highest-rated games so far, proving the Zelda franchise’s long-standing benchmark still holds up nearly 30 years later. sources.title: Hozy brings calm, tactile home restoration to PS5 on November 9
sources.text: Are you ready to meet your new cozy favourite? Imagine actually enjoying cleaning your house or ripping out old tiles. Unhinged, isn’t it? You put on your favourite music and open the windows to let the fresh air in. The dust disappears, the floor begins to shine with every sweep of the mop, and the rooms start to transform into cozy, welcoming spaces. There’s something incredibly satisfying about seeing it all come together, one step at a time. That’s exactly what we wanted to capture in Hozy – a cozy, tactile and stress-free home restoration game that is coming to PlayStation 5 on November 9. Hozy is a game where you can completely unwind. There are no timers, no scores and no pressure. Each level in Hozy features a space with its own atmosphere and story. Your first job is to tidy it up and renovate it. Then furnish it using the sets of furniture and décor provided. Don’t worry about being overwhelmed with an endless catalogue – each level features a carefully curated set of items you’ll need so that the end result always looks worthy of the interior design magazine. To help you tackle the tasks of refurbishing the rooms with ease, you’ll have access to an array of tools: from a simple mop to a crowbar. We all know what it’s like to mop the floors… But in Hozy, even this is a real pleasure. We’ve done our best to ensure that using each tool brings nothing but joy. You can also interact with the surroundings and a whole host of furniture. Open the window to let the breeze play with the dust particles. Light a lamp by the sofa to create a cosy reading nook. Play a tune on the piano or find secret messages in one of the drawers – experiment with different objects to discover what other interesting effects await you. Every surface, every object and instrument has its own unique sound. And the music changes dynamically as you progress through the level – we recommend playing with headphones or a home cinema system to fully appreciate the sounds of the world around you. This is something we’re particularly proud of. When we first started developing Hozy, our main aim was to make using the instruments as enjoyable and responsive as possible. And the DualSense wireless controller is simply perfect for complementing and enhancing that experience. Thanks to haptic feedback, interacting with objects and surfaces becomes even more realistic, as every action you take is accompanied by a unique set of vibrations. For example, when a mop glides smoothly across the floor or when you’re arranging furniture. Combined with the adaptive triggers, you’ll naturally feel the resistance of the floorboards as they finally give way to the crowbar. The DualSense’s built-in speaker helps you immerse yourself even further in the game’s atmosphere, subtly emitting additional sounds from the instruments you are currently using. Once you’ve completed the Hozy storyline, comprising nine unique levels, your journey into the world of cosiness isn’t over yet. Come back to the houses you’ve already restored to discover… new versions of the previous rooms. The ‘Game+’ mode will help you look at these rooms in a new light (literally) – now you can switch between day and night, as well as furnish rooms with different sets of furniture. Some of them will change beyond recognition. If you fancy creating something truly yours, Hozy has just the thing for you – a Sandbox mode with every item available in the game. Mix and match, duplicate, and customize your rooms however you wish. Who are we to tell you which wallpaper, background colour, window shape, support beams or light switches to choose? But there’s more: we also have plans for seasonal events and various DLCs, both free and paid. Of course, we haven’t forgotten about the various accessibility features, so that as many renovators as possible can enjoy Hozy. The game is available in 11 different languages and includes a range of visual and control settings. Adjust the movement speed of your tools, invert the camera, change colour display settings and much more. If you want to make playing Hozy even more comfortable – settle into your favourite armchair, pour yourself a cup of hot chocolate and launch the game on PlayStation Portal. We’re looking forward to November 9, when you’ll be able to enjoy Hozy at your own pace.

Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid of an unspecified number of developers, after furloughing its entire team and then hiring some of that staff back. As reported by the Star Wars website Bespin Bulletin, several designers of the acclaimed tactics game have taken to LinkedIn to announce that they have been let go by the studio. Among those affected are senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who worked on the game for three and a half years and has been on furlough for the past three and a half months. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote in a LinkedIn post . Other designers who lost their jobs include UI Engineer Tyler Eichten and senior quality assurance analyst Ryan Mosher , who spent two years at Firaxis and a further two years at 1047 Games before joining Bit Reactor in October 2024. It's been a tumultuous few months for Bit Reactor. In September, it was reported that the studio had furloughed up to 80% of its staff in the weeks leading up to Zero Company's launch, with the studio having reportedly "run out of most of its money" ahead of the game's launch. At the time, former senior technical artist Zachariah Scott said the project was built with "shocking austerity". Scott also accused Bit Reactor of "concealing the fact that the team was furloughed weeks ago" after the company made the announcement. Within a month, Zero Company had sold one million copies and Bit Reactor subsequently announced it had hired back some of its staff. In a statement posted on Bluesky, CEO Greg Foertsch stated that the furlough had been a response to "unexpected business developments outside of our control" and "necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as we can". sources.text: "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together." Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work. Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin . Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected. Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go. "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote . "It was a privilege to ship a game with you." Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release. The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month . Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible". It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week. In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review , we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: BioWare May Be Dead, But a Modder Has Rebuilt Mass Effect 3's Multiplayer Into the Legendary Edition
sources.text: When the Mass Effect Legendary Edition came out in 2021, it included the single player campaign of all three original games, along with all the DLC. But while all the story content you could ever want was included, Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode was conspicuously absent, despite having a dedicated fanbase. Now, just a few weeks after EA's shutdown of BioWare , a team of modders has successfully ported Mass Effect 3 's multiplayer to the Legendary Edition, with all the graphics and engine improvements that came with that re-release. The mod will be coming out on N7 Day – November 7th – and will be free to play, as long as you already own Mass Effect Legendary Edition. I also got a chance to sit down with Mgamerz, who runs the ME3Tweaks team that created the mod, to talk about Mass Effect 3, and about the state of modding in 2026. And if you want to download the mod yourself, it's available now on Nexus Mods. IGN: So, tell me a little bit about the project, and how you got started on basically porting the Mass Effect 3 multiplayer over to the Legendary Edition. Mgamerz: Yeah, so my dev team, ME3Tweaks, and I run it. We ported Pinnacle Station back in 2021. Crazy effort. I don't know how we got that done in a two-month timeframe. And then we were doing other projects for two years, and then near the end of me working on LE2 Randomizer, which is a randomizer for legendary Mass Effect 2, someone discovered a copy of the Citadel in Mass Effect 2. There's an area from the wards. I can't remember which game it was, but they found an area of the game that nobody knew about before, and you could load into and you're like, 'Well, this was clearly supposed to be something, and then they just never finished it.' It was a very early prototype. And it was like, 'Man, what if we could port something like that into another level?' And so I made this project called Project Wardle, Ward being the first part of it. (We have a bunch of stupid internal code names.) And I eventually made it so we could port a Mass Effect 2 level into Mass Effect 3, and we fixed up the cover, because cover is just an unbelievable nightmare. It's very important for enemies to be able to use it. Gameplay's a huge component of why Mass Effect 3 is fun. And we got that working and then I was like, 'Well, man, what if we could port the multiplayer levels?' Because we did it for Pinnacle Station. We ported the old game. But Pinnacle Station is mostly just reused assets from Mass Effect 1. Like 90% of it was just existing assets that they just reused. But multiplayer was totally different. It's like, yeah, none of this content exists. So the scope of work is just huge. So at the end of 2023, right as we finished LE2 Randomizer, literally on N7 day, I spun up a new Discord. I invited a couple people and they're like, 'What's this Discord about?' I'm like, 'We're going to do something stupid. We're going to port [Mass Effect 3] Multiplayer.' And those were the first two messages I ever sent. I have some screenshots of it. And then people were like, 'Yeah, you're joking, right?' And I'm like, 'No.' And then the last three years we've been working on it. It hasn't been constant. Last year I broke my arm, which set us back six to eight months. But for the first two years, it was tons of prototyping. Within the first month of this project, we actually had multiplayer working. It was a proof of concept. And then we spent the next two years getting audio to port, from a different version of the audio engine because they upgraded it. It's like we got shaders building, which was a total nightmare because BioWare compiled the game with a bunch of sources that don't ship with the game. And so we had to figure out 'how do we replicate that?' So that took a long time. And then it's like textures. We have a bunch more people that know how to do texture upscaling. The first two years is almost all prototype and then asset generation. We want to make it look good. We're planning stuff out, that kind of stuff. So that's really not how it started. IGN: So, you basically built from scratch again? Did you take assets from the original Mass Effect 3? Mgamerz: Oh yeah, the whole thing ports from it. It's not a one-to-one port. We're not just taking Mass Effect 3 multiplayer and dumping it into Legendary Edition and then, 'Hey guys, check out it's multiplayer, [as] you remember it.' Where we took a lot of extra steps, the lighting actually gets re-baked in Unreal Engine 4's light solver. Essentially what that means is, imagine you have a light bulb in a room and if you wanted to project what the lights would look like, a light beam's going to hit your microphone and it's going to cast a shadow. And then that light bounces off for you, goes into your closet and it bounces off and illuminates the closet a little bit from the inside. Unreal Engine 3 had a solver and that's how all of the lighting for all the Unreal Engine 3 games worked. But in Unreal Engine 4, they added like, 'Oh, we can do additional light bounces or we found a better statistical way to do light bounces.' And so you get crisper shadow edges or the more soft, like a grate covering on some maps. The light bounces through the grate, and unless you have super high resolution textures, it looks terrible. Mass Effect 3 is full of terrible light maps. If you look at them, you're like, 'Wow, it's just a big stair step of shadows and it looks bad.' And so we spent a lot of time upgrading that kind of stuff. I modded Mass Effect 3 multiplayer for eight years before Legendary Edition came out, and there's a bunch of stuff I was like, 'Wow, I didn't even realize three of the character classes don't even use the highest-quality mesh.' So it's like BioWare made the Geth Infiltrator, and they made it at a high quality where it has all the polygons and triangles. And then as you get further away from the camera, it gets less triangles, because you can't see as much detail. But BioWare was just like, 'We'r

sources.title: How Modders Spent Three Years Remastering Mass Effect 3’s Fantastic Multiplayer For Legendary Edition: ‘Let’s Do Something Stupid’
sources.text: Mass Effect 3 Mass Effect: Legendary Edition Mass Effect: Universe N7 Day When the Mass Effect: Legendary Edition remasters launched in 2021, they had just about everything you could have wanted from a modern-day port of BioWareâs sci-fi RPGs. There were, however, two major exemptions: the original gameâs Pinnacle Station DLC , and Mass Effect 3 âs cooperative multiplayer mode. In 2021, the ME3Tweaks modding group brought back Pinnacle Station . Now, five years later, itâs back to finish the job, and is releasing a remastered mod of the multiplayer mode for those who have the Legendary Edition on PC. The project began in earnest three years ago, with modder Mgamerz coming up with the idea shortly after wrapping up a randomizer mod for the Mass Effect 2 remaster. Luckily, the ME3Tweaks group had a lot of the foundations set in place to bring the missing mode into the Legendary Edition after years of working in the Mass Effect modding space. âThere was somebody who had shown that they could port a level when they found an unused level in [ Mass Effect 1 âs remaster],â he tells Kotaku . âThere was like an extra Citadel area, and I was like, âOh man, what if I could port that to another game?â Sometimes I just get these crazy ideas, like, âWhat if I just did something crazy?â And so I tried porting it, and I was able to actually get it to port because we did Pinnacle Station , so we had a lot of the infrastructure to do it, and I was able to port it. I’m like, âman, what if we could do like a multiplayer level?â And I was able to port, I think it was [Firebase] Condor. It’s one of the first DLC maps. ItÂ looked terrible, but you didn’t immediately crash the game loading into it. And I had already ported multiplayer levels before in my Redemption map pack that I had made from single player to multiplayer, so I kind of knew everything that was needed. And then it was like, âOkay, well, I made this map, but there’s no game mode; you can’t do anything on it. Really, it looks terrible.â And so I kind of shelved it for a couple of months.â After some time, Mgamerz decided he wanted to make a multiplayer mod, and thus went back to the original Mass Effect 3 , and says he was struck by how much âfurther advancedâ the groupâs modding tools had become while working on the remaster.Â âLiterally probably about three hours into it, I’m like, âThese tools suck,â and I say that as someone who helped write most of them. Our tooling for the original trilogy is so bad compared to what we got in Legendary Edition .â Part of that is because, prior to the remasterâs launch, the ME3Tweaks group had meetings with folks at BioWare about making the Legendary Edition more modder-friendly, and although the company wasnât able to implement everything, it did give the group a better starting point. âIt was probably just like a month before the game release,â he recalls. âWe gave them a list of some of the most awful things we have to deal with, and we kind of didn’t expect them to do most of the changes. And they didn’t. I mean, it’s one month before launch, so you can’t really make big changes. But they snuck a few in right at the end of development for us, which has helped a lot of single-player development. They gave us some information that we couldn’t really leverage until we started working on stuff like this, like how does DLC mount work? When the game loads, DLC mounts into the game, but in ME3 , it loads single-player versus multiplayer, and we didn’t really have any idea how any of that worked. So they gave us information about that, and then we, you know, over the years we built on top of it.â Over two years later, on November 7, 2023, Mgamerz created a Discord server for Project Milan, what would become the Mass Effect 3 Legendary Edition multiplayer remaster mod, telling the rest of the ME3Tweaks modders, “Let’s do something stupid. Let’s port multiplayer.” He says that development was on and off over the course of three years, citing some personal matters that got in the way including breaking his arm at some point during the whole effort, but the group had a working prototype of the mode as early as December of 2023.Â “You could pick at least one kit, and the game didn’t crash until you got to wave three,” he recalls. “Enemies would spawn. Audio was totally broken. Like there was virtually no audio. The shaders were all broken, so you just got checkerboards all over the place. But you could actually play it, and enemies spawn. You could kill them. You get points. sources.title: 20 anos de PlayStation Store: desenvolvedores revelam os jogos incríveis que mais os surpreenderam
sources.text: PlayStation Studios e desenvolvedores de terceiros comentam os jogos mais surpreendentes. Há 20 anos, a PlayStation Store conecta jogadores a jogos de todos os tipos e estilos, de grandes aventuras de sucesso a tesouros indies e tudo o que há entre eles. Para marcar a ocasião, convidamos desenvolvedores da PlayStation Studios e de estúdios de terceiros a refletirem sobre um jogo incrível dos últimos 20 anos que os tenha surpreendido. Não necessariamente o jogo favorito de todos, mas um que eles não esperavam gostar tanto quanto gostaram, ou que os conquistou de uma forma inesperada. Você também pode conferir a seleção especial 20 Anos de PlayStation Store , onde poderá explorar ofertas de jogos e uma curadoria com os maiores sucessos escolhidos a dedo. Agora, veja o que os desenvolvedores compartilharam sobre jogos dos últimos 20 anos que os surpreenderam: “O jogo que me vem à mente é Balatro. Embora seja baseado nas regras simples e familiares do pôquer, fiquei completamente fascinado com a sensação de satisfação que vem de ver suas pontuações aumentarem cada vez mais por meio do progresso e de diferentes combinações. É um jogo verdadeiramente envolvente que me faz lembrar por que os jogos são tão divertidos de jogar.” – Naoki Hamaguchi, diretor da série Final Fantasy VII Remake, Square Enix “Dragon Quest XI: Echos of an Elusive Age me surpreendeu na primeira vez que joguei. Tudo, desde a história até o design dos personagens e o mundo, tem um charme difícil de não se apaixonar. Sempre que o caminho à frente parecia claro, o jogo destruía a ilusão com uma reviravolta inesperada. É uma jornada heroica maravilhosa, com uma personalidade muito original.” – Jonathan Burke, Diretor Sênior de Tecnologia, Santa Monica Studio “Um jogo que eu não esperava gostar tanto quanto gostei foi God of War (2018). Ainda é inacreditável para mim que a Santa Monica Studio tenha conseguido realizar tal feito no PlayStation 4. Mas o que realmente me cativou foi a história. Nos jogos anteriores, God of War 1, 2 e 3, Kratos foi, na minha humilde opinião, definido em grande parte pela raiva e pela fúria, com pouquíssima profundidade emocional. Mas God of War (2018) mudou isso de forma substancial. Os temas de paternidade, autocontrole, ruptura de ciclos tóxicos, luto e identidade não estavam na minha lista de expectativas. No entanto, ele se saiu excepcionalmente bem em todos esses aspectos emocionais. Pouquíssimos jogos conseguiram equilibrar uma jogabilidade incrível com uma história profundamente envolvente da maneira como God of War (2018) conseguiu.” – Ramone Russell, Diretor, Comunicação de Desenvolvimento de Produtos e Estrategista de marca no San Diego Studio “Eu não estava preparado para Inscryption. Eu achava que era só um jogo de tabuleiro com cartas meio sinistro, mas resolvi experimentar porque, normalmente, adoro esse tipo de jogo. Achei fascinante e envolvente a complexidade da interação entre as cartas e seus modificadores. Como alguém que trabalha com jogos que possuem narrativas profundas e complexas, gostei do quanto o jogo confia em nós, jogadores, para desvendar a narrativa enigmática (e a mecânica de jogo!) por conta própria. Inscryption faz algo incrível: começa como um jogo aparentemente simples e direto, que recompensa a persistência ao revelar novas camadas de jogabilidade E de narrativa a cada passo. Isso também é muito especial para mim, pois nosso gatinho que partiu vive agora como o Build-a-Card ‘lil toot boi’. Descanse em paz, amiguinho.” – Arne Meyer, Diretor de Cultura e Comunicação, Naughty Dog “Inside, da Playdead, de alguma forma, foi lançado há mais de dez anos. Não possui interface nem diálogos e oferece uma experiência totalmente única, sem quaisquer instruções óbvias, meticulosamente elaborada para ensinar por meio de uma ‘mão invisível’, de forma que pareça natural e sem esforço. Os aspectos visuais e sonoros refletem perfeitamente a história ambígua que faz você refletir sobre ela por semanas (ou até uma década) após terminá-la. É uma obra-prima.” – Marcus Smith, Diretor Criativo, Insomniac Games “O jogo que me surpreendeu completamente foi Sayonara Wild Hearts! Eu não costumo me interessar por jogos que tenham elementos musicais e de ritmo como parte central da mecânica de jogo. Mas assim que vi este jogo em ação, ele realmente me cativou e me envolveu com seu estilo colorido e único. Assim que me envolvi com a história, ela passou a me atrair cada vez mais para o seu mundo, bem como para o cenário incrível e dinâmico. Logo percebi que estava completamente envolvido em um jogo musical e rítmico, e simplesmente não consegui largá-lo até terminar a história. A trilha sonora incrível foi o que me convenceu de vez. Eu com certeza recomendaria este jogo a qualquer pessoa que normalmente não jogue esse estilo; foi uma experiência verdadeiramente memorável para mim.” – Bruno Velazquez, Diretor de Jogo, Santa Monica Studio “Escolhi ‘Shadow of the Colossus’, lançado originalmente em 2005 para PlayStation 2. Só com seu cavalo e sua espada, você galopa pelas planícies em busca de criaturas gigantes para derrotá-las e salvar sua amada, que está mergulhada em um sono profundo. O jogo é, essencialmente, Davi contra Golias. Severa no início, a aventura celebra a solidão heroica com perfeição, apresentando batalhas épicas, um grande feito tecnológico e uma trilha sonora que entrou para a história. Uma obra-prima.” – Nicolas Doucet, diretor de estúdio, Team Asobi “Uncharted 2: Among Thieves (2009) foi o que mais me surpreendeu quando o joguei no PlayStation 3, pois, depois de tanta expectativa gerada pela demo, o jogo entregou algo ainda mais épico e impressionante. Cada sequência foi incrível: a qualidade da produção, o carisma do elenco e a sensação de estar jogando um filme de grande sucesso.
